newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says unable to track Russian space probe.
newsitem.headline: Australia says unable to track Russian space probe.

text.p: Australia is unable to track the Russian Mars space probe, which the White House says is expected to crash on east-central Australia around 0100 GMT on Monday, scientists said.

"The Russians take care of their own space craft. We do not have the equipment to track Russian space craft," said a spokesman at the Tidbinbilla satellite tracking station, Australia's premier space monitoring centre.
Len Ricardo, manager at Tidbinbilla, said all of Australia's space tracking facilities were geared to monitor United States space operations.
"It is not simply a matter of pointing a dish at it. All space craft use different radio frequencies and we are geared up to NASA," Ricardo told Reuters.
"I knew the space probe had not gone into a proper orbit, but I thought it would not be re-entering the earth's orbit for 30 days," he said.

The space craft contains reinforced canisters of deadly plutonium that pose a lethal threat if they crack open. The United States is prepared to offer all necessary assistance to any nation to deal with any resulting problems, a White House spokesman said.
